messages:
kevin: heads up — we got a spike of 429s from embeddings-prod around 09:12 UTC. Logs show `rate_limit_exceeded` and long queue times on node pool `embeddings-s` while `rerank-p` has spare capacity. Investigating whether admission control is misrouting or lanes are imbalanced.

maria: can you paste the alert id / graph? is this new? :thinking_face:

kevin: alert `SRE_EMB_QUEUE_HIGH` -> fired at 09:08 (15m). small snippet from logs: ```[09:12:06] request_id=abc123 status=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded lane=embeddings-s queue_ms=2400```

thomas: I can see the dashboard — embeddings-s queue length jumped to ~180, average latency for embedding calls up x4. rerank-p CPU/GPU utilization is ~25%. Looks like the admission controller sent too many small-embeddings to the embeddings-s lane.

jess: was there a recent rollout for routing policy? I remember a routing tweak yesterday to prefer cheaper quantized variants, maybe that touched embeddings routing.

kevin: there was a minor change to routing table at 02:00 UTC to consolidate some lanes. I rolled it back quickly but maybe stale connections kept going to embeddings-s.

ops-oncall: I'm seeing many short lived connections from a single client id (team-internal loadtester) hammering small-size embeddings. Could be an unthrottled flood. I've limited that client via API-key quota for now. :white_check_mark:

maria: good stop-gap. We should also add a hard cap at the edge for per-client qps for embeddings to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

thomas: agreed. Proposed action list: 1) keep client quota enforced (done), 2) move 30% of new requests to rerank-p by adjusting routing weights, 3) add admission-control token-bucket tuned to GPU capacity per-lane, 4) add an explicit dedicated small-embeddings lane for very high-QPS tiny vectors.

kevin: immediate change — bumped rerank-p weight by 0.3 (experiment flag `route_override/emb_move_20260318`). Monitoring now. Dashboards show queue falling to ~60 in 5m.

sre-bot: ALERT update: `SRE_EMB_QUEUE_HIGH` status -> recovering at 09:27 UTC.

jess: for the longer term we need cost analysis. If we create a separate tiny-embed lane (more small, higher throughput, possible bfloat quantization), what's the unit cost delta vs shared lane? ops-oncall, can you do a rough monthly delta?

ops-oncall: will run numbers, but preliminary: dedicated small-embed lane w/ more aggressive batching reduces GPU token cost by ~20% for tiny vectors, but introduces an extra GPU reservation cost. Net depends on commit utilization. I'll send a short estimate in #finance later today.

maria: also add regression alert to catch routing config drift — require a canary period where routing changes don't increase queue length > 30% for 10m.

kevin: agreed. I'll follow up with a PR to the routing service to add admission-control per-lane and start a RFC for tiny-embed lane. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:

thomas: leaving a note to run an offline replay of yesterday's traffic against proposed lanes to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.

kevin: logging the incident in incidents/ with link once I finish writeup.

sre-bot: Deploy bot: `route-service` rollback completed at 09:45 UTC (rev 7f4c -> 7f3e).
